(1) Vide this judgment/award, I shall decide the Detailed Accident Report (DAR) which was treated as a claim petition U/s 166 of The Motor Vehicle Act 1988 (MV Act in short) filed for compensation on account of injuries sustained by the injured/petitioner Kunti Ahirwar in a road vehicular accident which took place on 31.05.2023.
Case Set up in the DAR (2) In the DAR itself the detailed description of the accident has not been mentioned.

In the Interim Accident Report (IAR) in column 10 pertaining to brief description of the accident, it is averred that the injured/petitioner Ms. Kunti was doing work with her associate on the road divider near Air Force Station MB Road, Sangam Vihar when suddenly she was hit by a bike rider and she sustained injury.
(3) A more detailed version is found in the copy of the charge-sheet which is annexed alongwith the DAR wherein the statement of the petitioner has been reproduced.

Inter-alia the petitioner stated that on 31.05.2023 at about 9 am she was installing iron grills on the divider at MB Road in front of Air Force Station when a motorcyclist driving his vehicle at a high speed and carelessly came and hit the petitioner due to which the petitioner became unconscious.
Upon regaining consciousness, the petitioner found that she was admitted in the hospital, where she was treated.
The petitioner thereafter went to the police station with her husband and friend Ms. Radha.

At the police station,
the petitioner's friend Ms. Radha saw the respondent no.1 driver and recognized him as being the person who caused the Kunti Ahirwar Vs Rijwan & Anr MACT No. 396/2023 Page No.4 of 23 accident and had taken the petitioner to the hospital.

Certain principles for delineating just compensation were enumerated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Raj Kumar Vs Ajay Kumar & Ors (2011) 1 SCC 343 as follows - "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4.

sentences.text: The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the petitioner to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be Kunti Ahirwar Vs Rijwan & Anr MACT No.
396/2023 Page No.11 of 23 compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the petitioner, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
Assessment of pecuniary damages under item (i) and under item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence.
Award under the head of future medical expenses - item (iii) -- depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof.

Assessment of non-pecuniary damages - items (iv), (v) and (vi) -- involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the petitioner and the effect thereof on the future life of the petitioner."

Award towards medical expenses /treatment (34)

The petitioner/PW-1 claimed to have spent Rs.2,00,000/- in her medical treatment however she candidly admitted in her cross-examination conducted by Ld. counsel for the respondent no. 1 that she had not filed any bill of medical treatment of Rs.2,00,000/-.

The only medical document of the petitioner on record is the discharge summary of HAH Centenary Hospital Ex.PW1/1 as per which the petitioner was medically treated the same day and not admitted in the hospital as such.
No discharge summary is on record and the column pertaining to date of admission is left blank.
The petitioner has not examined any medical expert who could opine that the petitioner was advised bed rest post the accident.
The petitioner also did not examine her employer who could have deposed about the leaves if any taken by the petitioner post the accident.
In such circumstances, the petitioner can only be awarded amount qua the actual period of treatment/hospitalization i.e. for one day.
The minimum per day wage rate prescribed by the Government of NCT of Delhi during the relevant period was Rs.663/-.

(50) The fact of the matter is that the accident took place on 31.05.2023 i.e. after the coming into force of the amendment to Section 166 (3) MV Act with effect from 01.04.2022.

(51) The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Go Digit General Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Mohd. Javed through Shehnaz and Ors. MAC.APP. 416/2025 and CM Appl. 39671/2025 decided on 09.07.2025 observed in paragraph no. 5 as follows- "5.

sentences.text: So far as concerns the award of recovery rights, clearly that appears to be an inadvertent error by the learned Trial Court since, after the amendment to Section 166 (3) of the MV Act with effect from 01.04.2022 which is the provision for grant of recovery rights is no longer available in the statute book."
(52) This court is bound by the aforesaid observation of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.

The accident having occurred post the coming into effect of the amendment to Section 166 (3) MV Act, the principle of pay and recover is inapplicable and the respondent insurance company is required to be exonerated in view of the fundamental breach of the terms of the insurance policy committed by the respondent no. 1.
(53) Thus, the liability to pay the award amount falls squarely and solely upon the respondent no. 1 driver cum owner being the principal tortfeasor.

This view was reiterated by the Apex Court in the subsequent judgment of Mangla Ram Vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors (2018) 5 SCC 656 .
(23) Additionally, in the case of the Chola Mandalam M. S. General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him.
The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the petitioner to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
